description: US ZIP code for the project site. Used for soil thermal properties and climate zone lookup.
notes: 5-digit US ZIP only. Non-US sites not supported in v1.

description: DOE prototype building type. Determines baseline load profile, floor area, and occupancy schedule.
notes: Options: small_office, medium_office, large_office, primary_school, secondary_school, standalone_retail, retail_stripmall, warehouse, outpatient_healthcare

description: Total conditioned floor area across all floors. Footprint = floor_area / num_floors.
notes: Leave blank to use DOE prototype default. Must be > 10 m².

description: Number of above-grade floors. Used to compute building footprint for borefield layout.
notes: Affects footprint area and borehole field sizing. Leave blank for prototype default.

description: Year the building was built or last major envelope renovation. Used for building age adjustment.
notes: Tiers: pre-1980 (leaky), 1980–2005 (standard), 2006–present (modern/code). Set 0 for planned/new construction.

description: Glazing quality tier. Bundles U-factor and SHGC. SHGC dominates cooling load sensitivity (13× more than U-factor per EnergyPlus study).
notes: Options: triple_low_e (annual loads ×0.77–0.91 vs baseline), double_low_e (baseline), double_pane (×0.98–1.24), single_pane (×2.24 heat / ×1.29 cool). Ranges from 8-city × 3-type sensitivity study.

description: Air tightness of the building envelope. Dominates heating load in cold climates.
notes: Options: tight (annual heating ×0.81 vs baseline), standard (baseline), leaky (annual heating ×1.57). From EnergyPlus sensitivity study.

description: Window-to-wall ratio. Fraction of exterior wall area that is glazed. Affects solar gain and conduction loss. Baseline is 20%; each 10pp increase adds ~3–5% to annual cooling load.
notes: Range 0.10–0.90. At wwr=70%: annual heating ×1.45, annual cooling ×1.26 vs wwr=20% baseline. From EnergyPlus sensitivity study.

description: Center-to-center spacing between boreholes in the field.
notes: Typical range 5–8 m. Closer spacing causes thermal interference between boreholes over time.

description: Shape of the borehole field layout. Affects how many boreholes fit in the available footprint.
notes: Options: square (1:1), elongated (9:1 — for hotel/linear wing)

description: Preferred average borehole depth. Optimizer may go deeper if footprint is constrained.
notes: Minimum 100 m (required). Typical US range 100–150 m. Deeper = fewer boreholes needed but higher drilling cost.

description: Expert override: fix the borehole count instead of letting the optimizer determine it.
notes: Leave blank in normal use. Only override if site survey has determined a fixed field size.

description: Confidence in the soil thermal conductivity estimate. Affects best/base/worst cost range width.
notes: Options: high (lab test available), medium (regional estimate), low (no site data)
